clue.text: They go head-over-heels, wanting glasses

explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats who somersault are called this, and so are straight-sided drinking glasses.

clue.text: Reduce volume of refuse

definitions.meaning: to lower the sound on a radio

explanation.definitionFit: Lowering a dial is to lessen sound; to decline an offer is also this phrase.

clue.text: Totally exploits fish in the drink

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit it to the full
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone drains every last bit from a fish in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' suggests the sea, where fish live, but it is a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A frothy beverage of milk and flavouring is a drink.

clue.text: A better bed

definitions.meaning: one who lays bets, a punter
a stratum or bed of rock

explanation.definitionFit: One who lays a wager is a gambler; a stratum or bed is a level in rock.

clue.text: It's ever on the move, being fidgety

indicators.note: on the move means these letters are moved about and rearranged

parts.note: the letters ITS from it's are fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is constantly moving and restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless and unable to keep still, as a skittish horse is.

clue.text: A scientist's innovative style

parts.note: innovative means new
ton is an old word for fashionable style

explanation.surface: A researcher shows off a fresh way of working.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for style or fashion is a crossword favourite, as in 'the ton', high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist who formulated the laws of motion and gravity.

clue.text: Promptitude in installing listening equipment around bars

indicators.note: around means the listening organs are placed on either side of the bars

parts.note: ears are what we listen with
lines, as in bars of a stave or prison bars

explanation.surface: A quick installation of eavesdropping devices near pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening equipment' suggests bugs or headphones; it is simply EARS. 'in installing' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being early or prompt means acting in good time.

clue.text: To tear into the heartless is just foolishness

indicators.note: into means the tearing word goes inside the shortened word
heartless means the central letter of the word the is removed

parts.note: the article, before its middle is taken out
to tear is to rip

explanation.surface: Ripping into heartless people is just silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle letter, leaving TE; 'into' sets the tearing word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish or nonsense, in British slang, is the same word as the cooked stomach lining.

clue.text: Cancel Geordie's pass?

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle, in the North East, NE
a gate is a pass or way through, as in a mountain gate

explanation.surface: A Newcastle native's permit is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a person from Tyneside in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify or invalidate something is to cancel it.

clue.text: Fish requiring urgent treatment

indicators.note: treatment means these letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish is rushed to the vet.
explanation.definitionFit: The gurnard, a spiny sea fish, also goes by this name.

clue.text: Broadcast on the subject of strain

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
a strain is a tune or song, and a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A transmission is reported about some kind of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress, but here it is a musical strain, a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on a transmission, as from a satellite, is to send it onward as a broadcast.

clue.text: Being quick to squeal about hot food

indicators.note: about means one piece is put around the other, so the word for squealing wraps the food

parts.note: to squeal on someone is to inform, to sing
curry is a spicy hot dish

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to inform on the spicy meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeal' looks like a noise but is slang for informing to the police; 'about' splits that word around the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing about hurriedly means moving fast, as small animals do when they dart.

clue.text: Leaving, as one's tired out

indicators.note: out signals that these letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of one's, ONES, are part of the fodder
taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone quits because they are exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns ONES and TIRED into the answer's letters; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning a post or partner is the act of going away from it.

clue.text: Into Oriental exercises, but somewhat clumsy

parts.note: into gives in
E for east, the Orient
PT is physical training, exercises

explanation.surface: Someone keen on Eastern exercise regimes turns out awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is the old British school name for gym classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward or lacking skill describes someone bungling a task.

clue.text: Argue like a mathematician?

definitions.meaning: to argue noisily or at length
a ... is a top Cambridge mathematics graduate, so behaving as one is jokingly to do what ... do

explanation.definitionFit: Quarrelling at length is disputing; the Cambridge maths title of wrangler gives the joke.

clue.text: Look daggers about objective Welsh leader

indicators.note: about means the angry look goes around the target

parts.note: to look daggers is to glower
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A Welsh chief glares at his goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Owain Glyndwr (Glendower) led a Welsh revolt against the English around 1400.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen Glendower led the Welsh rebellion against Henry IV and appears in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Such a belief is held by the married

indicators.note: held by means the word is goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Married couples share a particular faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in a god or gods is a creed, the opposite of atheism.

clue.text: The curmudgeon fell over a stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a fell is an animal skin or hide
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: A grumpy man tripped over a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a past tense of fall; it is a hide, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who hates spending is a tight-fisted grump.

clue.text: Truly conned, though far from ill-informed

parts.note: well means truly or thoroughly
to con is to study, so conned means read

explanation.surface: Someone was truly tricked, yet is no fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conned' suggests swindled; here it is the old verb con, to study or read.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledgeable from much reading means the opposite of ignorant.

clue.text: Puff about English authoress

indicators.note: about means the puffing word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to puff up is to swell

explanation.surface: A writer is puffed up about Englishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Sewell was the Victorian novelist who wrote Black Beauty, a woman writer.

clue.text: A person putting up with others

definitions.text: A person putting up with others

parts.words: A person putting up with others
parts.note: reads as someone tolerant, but means someone staying in a house with others, as a paying tenant

explanation.definitionFit: A paying tenant in another's house is put up there, sharing with the household.

clue.text: Underworld boss, fellow to loathe

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god ruling the underworld
a fellow is an equal, a like, as in 'we shall not see his like again'

explanation.surface: A gangland chief and his associate are hated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but it is Dis, the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Hating something is to have a strong aversion to it.

clue.text: Beasts holding police officers? That settles it!

indicators.note: holding means the animals wrap around the police

parts.note: deer are wild animals
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, plain-clothes police

explanation.surface: Animals catch detectives in a final game.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A final game that settles a contest is a deciding match.

clue.text: Soporific work — I scoffed

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A dull work makes someone wolf down food.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleep-inducing drug derived from opium is a narcotic sedative.

clue.text: Crave a little money to get ahead

parts.note: P is a penny, a small coin
being in the lead means being ahead

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a small sum to get on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or implore earnestly is to crave, in its old sense of asking for.

clue.text: Bird we finally notice round river?

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word we
round means the noticing word goes around the river's abbreviation

parts.note: to get something is to grasp or notice it

explanation.surface: We at last spot a bird by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: E (the end of 'we') comes first, then GET wrapped round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron is a wading bird.

clue.text: Misleading one in deft clue construction

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
construction means the letters are built into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a tricky clue built cleverly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction' gives DECETFUL, the clue's two words rearranged, and 'in' places the numeral inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceptive or dishonest describes something intended to give a false impression.

clue.text: Children matter

definitions.meaning: a topic or question under discussion

explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's progeny in legal terms; a subject under debate is a point at stake.

clue.text: The ending of a quarrel

parts.note: a quarrel is also a crossbow bolt, and its pointed tip is the end of it

explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a crossbow bolt, whose sharpened tip is at its far end.

clue.text: Criticise waders

definitions.meaning: to make sniping remarks, sly attacks

explanation.definitionFit: Sly sniping remarks are criticism, and the bird of that name is a long-billed wader.

clue.text: Resent breaking of records

indicators.note: breaking of means the word is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resents broken sporting records.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something into a ledger or log is to put it on record.

clue.text: Stayed in custody

definitions.meaning: halted or checked, as a disease's progress is stayed

explanation.definitionFit: Checked or halted is stayed; taken by police means held in custody.
